name: Netherlands
headline_status: Cannabis remains technically illegal in the Netherlands, but small-scale possession and sales in licensed coffee shops are tolerated for adults 18+.
summary: Under the Dutch toleration policy, prosecutors do not pursue possession of up to 5 g, and municipalities may allow coffee shops that sell no more than 5 g per transaction to adults. Supply to coffee shops has long been illegal, so the state is testing a legal, regulated supply chain in 10 municipalities; that experiment's main phase began on 7 April 2025. Medicinal cannabis is supplied to pharmacies through the government's Office of Medicinal Cannabis.

possession_limit.value: Up to 5 g of cannabis or hash is tolerated and not prosecuted.

home_grow.value: Growing up to 5 plants is still illegal, but police usually only seize them; more than 5 plants leads to prosecution.

purchase_age.value: 18; coffee shops must check customers' age.

retail_sales.value: Tolerated coffee shops may sell up to 5 g per transaction if they cause no nuisance, sell no hard drugs, do not sell to minors and do not advertise; municipalities decide whether and how many shops are allowed.

medical_program.value: The government's Office of Medicinal Cannabis holds a monopoly on supplying medicinal cannabis, which it delivers only to pharmacies, dispensing GPs, hospitals and vets.

regulator.value: Ministry of Justice and Security with the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport (Youth, Prevention and Sport minister) for the supply-chain experiment; municipalities license coffee shops; Office of Medicinal Cannabis for medical supply.

tourists.value: National rules have limited coffee shop sales to Dutch residents since 1 January 2013, but enforcement of this residence criterion varies by municipality.

timeline.event: Residence criterion introduced: coffee shops may only sell to Dutch residents
Senate approves closed coffee shop chain experiment bill
Experiment start-up phase begins in Breda and Tilburg
Transition phase starts in all 10 participating municipalities
Experimental phase begins: participating coffee shops may sell only regulated, legally grown cannabis

faq.q: Is weed legal in the Netherlands?
faq.a: Not technically. It is tolerated: possession of up to 5 g is not prosecuted and licensed coffee shops may sell small amounts to adults.

faq.q: Can tourists buy weed in Amsterdam?
faq.a: National policy restricts coffee shop sales to Dutch residents, but each municipality decides how strictly that rule is enforced, so access for visitors depends on the city.

faq.q: What is the Dutch weed experiment?
faq.a: A trial in 10 municipalities in which coffee shops sell only cannabis from licensed growers, testing a fully legal supply chain. Its experimental phase began on 7 April 2025.
